properties.validity: Pressure is kinematic throughout this solver, which is the commonest unit error when a component model is coupled to it. The quadratic form is written odd, `Q` times the absolute value of `Q`, never `Q` squared: the even form makes the reverse branch a positive-feedback runaway

properties.name: Fan affinity laws
properties.validity: Geometric similarity, fixed diameter, Reynolds number high enough that efficiency does not move with speed; fails at deep turndown. The correction is applied at every evaluation, not once: a 40 C return is 6.4 per cent less dense than the 20 C a curve is usually measured at

total efficiency, greater than zero and at most one

properties.name: Porous jump, a resistive face

inertial resistance, half the inertial coefficient times thickness

properties.name: Tile loss coefficient from open-area ratio

symbols.meaning: loss coefficient on the approach velocity
open-area ratio, greater than zero and at most one

properties.validity: Thin-plate form, referred to the approach velocity. It gives 30.68 at a quarter open, 4.370 at half and 2.937 at 0.56 — the gates are the two limits, `K` to zero as `sigma` approaches one and `K` to infinity as `sigma` approaches zero, and the specification records that a quoted value of about 4 at 0.56 is contradicted by the formula. The derived `K` is always printed
properties.citation: Idelchik, Handbook of Hydraulic Resistance, 4th ed., Begell (2007) — paywalled; the formula as transcribed in this project's own specification

properties.name: Rack Cooling Index
properties.validity: 100 per cent means no inlet is outside the recommended band at all; zero means every inlet sits at the allowable limit. **The value depends on which sample points are used**, so the sample set is part of the definition and is reported with the number. The low-side form is the mirror, with a recommended-low minus allowable-low denominator. The envelope is stored in Celsius and converted to kelvin before comparison
properties.citation: Herrlin, "Rack cooling effectiveness in data centers and telecom central offices: the Rack Cooling Index", ASHRAE Transactions 111(2) (2005) 725-731, no DOI — paywalled; the formula as transcribed in this project's own specification

properties.name: Return Temperature Index

symbols.meaning: mean air temperature rise across the IT equipment

properties.validity: Below 100 per cent is bypass, above is recirculation, 100 is ideal. At steady state with all IT heat leaving through the return it equals the ratio of IT mass flow to supply mass flow, so **halving the supply flow exactly doubles it, whatever the geometry** — a gate that needs no external data. The two temperatures must be flux-weighted patch means, never area means
properties.citation: Herrlin, "Airflow and cooling performance of data centers: two performance metrics", ASHRAE Transactions 114(2) (2008) 182-187, no DOI — paywalled; the formula as printed in the LBNL self-benchmarking guide

properties.name: Supply and Return Heat Index

symbols.meaning: pre-heat picked up by the cold air before it reaches the racks
useful heat pickup at the racks

properties.validity: `SHI` approaching zero is ideal. The implementation forms the denominator once and subtracts, so the two sum to exactly one in floating point — a property of the implementation, gated as such. Here `Q` is the stated rack power, not a measured mass flow times a measured rise, so the pair holds only under the heat-zone modelling assumption
properties.citation: Sharma, Bash & Patel, "Dimensionless parameters for evaluation of thermal design and performance of large-scale data centers", AIAA 2002-3091, DOI 10.2514/6.2002-3091 — paywalled; the form as carried in this project's own specification

One curve per whole patch, corrected for density and speed at every evaluation. A curve with fewer than two points, a non-increasing flow column, a rising pressure branch, a non-positive maximum pressure or flow, a non-positive curve density or speed, or an efficiency outside the half-open unit interval is refused by name in `FanCurve::validate`. A fan condition on any field but pressure is structurally impossible: only the fan module rewrites the triple.

properties.reason: Splitting an existing internal face into a coincident pair of boundary faces is a topology mutation this solver does not perform. The two routes that exist are to emit the coincident pair at mesh-generation time, or to model the plenum as a separate region and use the boundary form. A jump on an ordinary internal face needs no baffle; what it cannot do is make the scalars jump, which is the only thing a baffle adds. The case key exists so that this refusal can fire.
properties.permissiveFallback: Under the permissive switch the refusal returns an empty internal-face jump, and the caller **discards it**: the tile falls through to its ordinary lowering and becomes a boundary porous jump on the same patch, with the scalars continuous. The behaviour is safe; the comment above the call site describes it wrongly, and D1 fixes that comment.

properties.reason: A fan patch makes a face neither uniformly Dirichlet nor uniformly Neumann, and a jump makes the coefficient non-constant, so the direct Fourier pressure path is not available on a room that has either. The rank-one correction that would put it back is named and not implemented.

A saturation-constrained source with its own inner iteration is a different model. What is offered instead: supersaturation is reported with a cell count and the worst excess, and the case may set a barometric pressure, virtual temperature, a fan supply relative humidity and a tile plenum relative humidity. No case key reaches this refusal today, so it is documented rather than fired.

The supply-temperature sweep key is parsed and never read, so the free-cooling ceiling is absent from every report. This is the defect class the case format exists to prevent, live in the shipped format. D4 implements it; the first files to change are `rust/src/io/case_dc.rs`, where the key is read, and `rust/src/bin/datacentre.rs`, where the ceiling is written.
